claim_boundary: Thirty juvenile fencers aged 11-14 with four to five years of experience, randomly allocated ten per control, visual-feedback, and haptic-feedback group. Sixty rows represent the same 30 participants at Week 0 and Week 5, with three measurements per visit; they are not 60 athletes or 180 independent samples. Weapon is not reported. Lower unbalance percentages indicate improvement, while movement time is a separate speed outcome. Small groups, one club, minors, and five weeks prevent population, injury-prevention, or general coaching claims.
source_anomalies: Table S4 omits the printed control-group Week 5 movement-time average; the ten participant rows compute to 9.928 seconds, matching the article table.
Derived Tables S10-S12 contain reversed week columns, a VG7 typo, and mislabeled haptic-group headings; they are excluded rather than treated as extra observations.
